references.text: The Lord commands Moses to carve two new stone tablets like the first ones, which is the direct context for verse 4 where Moses carries out this command.
Moses broke the first stone tablets when he saw the golden calf, making the new tablets mentioned in 34:4 necessary.
Describes the original stone tablets that God gave Moses on Mount Sinai, which Moses now must replace.
God calls Moses up the mountain to receive the first stone tablets, parallel to Moses' ascent in 34:4.
The Lord came down on Mount Sinai and called Moses up, a previous ascent to the same mountain.
Moses recounts how he carved two new stone tablets and went up the mountain, a parallel account to Exodus 34:4.
Moses tells that he threw the two tablets and broke them, the background for why new tablets had to be made.
Refers to the two stone tablets that Moses placed in the ark at Horeb, linking to the tablets Moses carried with him.
Mentions the ark of the covenant which contained the stone tablets, a New Testament reference to the tablets of the law.
Contrasting movements (up/down) with the tablets illustrate the transition from breaking the covenant to restoration.
The same event told in two different books; Deuteronomy confirms and comments on the action in Exodus.
Direct confirmation: Deuteronomy confirms that Moses carried out the specific action described in Exodus.
Complementary moments in the same chapter showing the entire process from preparation to receiving God's word.
